The planning dealt with here is concerned with the buildings and
spaces, both open and enclosed, that are required by the Univer-
sity to accomplish its expressed academic and professional goals.
Such an enterprise recognizes the relationship that exists among
the several levels of plan preparation and implementation: the
formulation of University objectives and policy, fiscal and admin-
istrative planning, planning for the long-range development of
the physical environment, and identification and use of the means
for implementation

The Social Sciences area between 38th and Walnut Streets and Locust Walk
will accommodate the Graduate School of Education, the School of Social Work
and some SAS departments now there, but in new buildings on a reconfigured
site. The intersection of the SAS area with the Wharton School area across
Locust Walk reflects the two schools' shared interest in the social sciences; an
overlap with the Annenberg School to the east relates to shared curriculum in
dramatic and performance arts.

of educational choice stregthened by the proximity of graduate and research pro-
grams and a primary commitment to the generation of new knowledge, new insights,
and, in the arts, new forms of creative expression. That paper also reviewed
the current context of higher education in the United States: the declining
pool of potential undergraduates, the problems of labor-intensive endeavors
caught in an inflationary spiral , and the nature of university planning in an
